Deterministic.description: A deterministic forecast: one horizon-length array per window, windows stepping by `interval`. One of a closed set of six canonical time series types owned by the data layer. This schema records the association and its metadata; the dense values live in the store named by `uri`.

application_data.description: Opaque, package-owned payload (typically JSON) carried verbatim for an application to reconstruct its own domain objects. Never parsed or interpreted here, and end users are not expected to set it. Element typing does not belong here — that is `element_type`.

array_shape.description: Full native shape of the stored array, in the order the store holds it: the first axis is the array's length and the trailing axes end with `element_shape`. Static types are `[length, *element_shape]`; a deterministic forecast stacks windows as `[horizon_count, count, *element_shape]`; probabilistic and scenarios forecasts add a percentile or scenario axis in front of that. Optional, and redundant for the static types, where it is exactly `[length] + element_shape`. It earns its place on the forecasts, whose array layout is a convention the producing package owns rather than a rule this layer enforces, so the stored geometry cannot be reconstructed from `horizon`, `count`, `percentiles`, and `scenario_count` alone. A consumer that has it should prefer it; one that does not falls back to those fields, which is exact for the static types and a best effort for the forecasts.

association_id.description: Surrogate id of this association, minted by the store that holds it. Assigned once when the association is created and never changed: renaming the series or reassigning its owner leaves it alone, so a consumer may persist it as a durable reference. Ids are never reused, and they are store-local — resolve one against the same store the document was exported from, not against an independently built store. Assigned by the store, never by a document author.

component_field.description: The field on the owning component or supplemental attribute whose value these values are the time-varying form of (e.g. max_active_power, rating). Free-form: it names a field in the consumer's own object model. Records what the values are for, where `name` only says which series they are.

count.description: Number of forecast windows. Descriptive, not part of the series' identity.

data_hash.description: Content hash of the stored array: SHA-256, hex-encoded. Optional — not every producer computes it.

element_shape.description: Per-step element shape: the trailing dims after time. An empty array means a scalar element.

element_type.description: What one timestep's values mean and how they are laid out. The physical dtype of the stored bytes derives from this and is not recorded separately. Unlike `units` and `quantity_kind` this is not a user-facing label — the writing package derives it from the array.

features.description: User-defined key/value tags that are part of the series' identity: two series differing only by a feature are distinct series. Feature names that collide with a field of a series or of the tuple addressing one are rejected.

horizon.description: Length of one forecast window. Descriptive, not part of the series' identity.

initial_timestamp.description: Start of the first forecast window. Written in one of two RFC 3339 forms, with at most 3 fractional-second digits: `date-time`, with `Z` or a UTC offset, names an instant; `date-time-local`, with no offset, is a wall clock and names no instant. `time_reference` fixes the form: `zoneless` requires `date-time-local`, `utc` requires a zero offset, and a fixed offset or an IANA zone requires `date-time`. With no `time_reference`, either form is accepted and none is assumed.

interval.description: Step between the start of consecutive forecast windows. Part of the series' identity: two forecasts of one variable at the same resolution but different intervals — a day-ahead and a real-time forecast — are distinct series. `PT0S` is the canonical interval of a single-window forecast, which has no second window to step to.

interval_alignment.description: Position of each timestamp in the period it represents.

name.description: Time series name (e.g. max_active_power). Part of the series' identity, and often carrying a disambiguating suffix; `component_field` records what the values are for.

owner_category.description: Whether the owner is a component or a supplemental attribute.

owner_id.description: ID of the owning component or supplemental attribute. The producing data layer allocates both from one id stream, so an `owner_id` never collides across the two categories; `owner_category` remains required because the store's catalog contract still supports independent streams from other producers, and it is still the store's disambiguator.

owner_type.description: Type name of the owning entity. Descriptive, not part of the series' identity.

per_unit_of.description: The field on the owning component that the values are a fraction of when `unit_system` is COMPONENT_BASE (e.g. base_power, storage_capacity). Completes the per-unit declaration: it names which of the owner's fields converts the values back to natural units, so a consumer need not know the owner's conventions. Free-form: it names a field in the consumer's own object model, and nothing here checks it against `unit_system`. Not part of the series' identity.

quantity_kind.description: Kind of physical quantity the values measure (e.g. ActivePower, ReactivePower, ElectricalEnergy). Coarser than `units` but finer than a dimension: ActivePower, ReactivePower, and ApparentPower share the dimension {M:1,L:2,T:-3}, so a dimension cannot tell them apart and a quantity kind can. It is also the only record of what the values measure when `unit_system` is a per-unit basis.

resolution.description: Cadence within a forecast window. Always present for a forecast, and part of the series' identity.

time_reference.description: How this series' timestamps were spelled, so a read hands back what the write declared instead of relabelling everything UTC. Absent means unspecified, which is not a claim the timestamps were written as UTC.

time_series_type.description: Discriminator. Fixed to Deterministic for this schema, pinned with `const` to match this repo's existing discriminators (Core/common.json's `curve_type`), which generate a plain string literal in both toolchains.

unit_system.description: Basis the series values are already expressed in. A declaration, not a conversion: nothing here rescales values, and converting a COMPONENT_BASE series back to natural units needs the owning component's field that `per_unit_of` names. Absent means unspecified, which is deliberately not the same as NATURAL_UNITS.

units.description: Unit label for the series values. Set by whoever creates the series and returned unchanged; not part of the series' identity, so two series differing only in this label are duplicates. Meaningless on its own when `unit_system` is a per-unit basis, where the values are dimensionless. By convention drawn from the unit vocabulary in Core/units.json, though this field is a free-text label the store does not validate against it.

uri.description: Locator for the dense data, unique within one store. No required format — typically a file path or an HDF5 dataset path; the backing store decides what it means and resolves it (infrastore uses its content hash as this value). Never parsed or interpreted here. This layer records where the values are, never the values.

DeterministicSingleTimeSeries.description: A synthetic deterministic forecast derived from a SingleTimeSeries by `transform_single_time_series`. array_shape.description: Full native shape of the stored array, in the order the store holds it: the first axis is the array's length and the trailing axes end with `element_shape`. InterruptibleStandardLoad.description:
An interruptible, voltage-dependent ZIP load whose demand can be curtailed through demand response programs, subject to an interruption cost.

Like `StandardLoad`, it breaks the ZIP into three pieces: Z (constant impedance), I (constant current), and P (constant power), according to `P = P_P * V^0 + P_I * V^1 + P_Z * V^2` for active power and `Q = Q_P * V^0 + Q_I * V^1 + Q_Z * V^2` for reactive power. (Voltage V is in per unit.) Unlike `StandardLoad`, it carries an `operation_cost` for interrupting the load.

For a non-interruptible ZIP load, see `StandardLoad`. For an interruptible constant-power load, see `InterruptiblePowerLoad`.

NonSequentialTimeSeries.description: An irregular static time series, sampled at explicit timestamps rather than on a grid. Deliberately carries neither `initial_timestamp` nor `resolution`: an irregular series has no fixed cadence and its key holds no timestamp. The timestamp vector itself lives in the store rather than here, content-addressed so that many irregular series sharing one time axis store it once; `timestamps_uri` names which axis this series sits on, so a document plus the store's arrays describe the series completely.

application_data.description: Opaque, package-owned payload (typically JSON) carried verbatim for an application to reconstruct its own domain objects. Never parsed or interpreted here, and end users are not expected to set it. Element typing does not belong here — that is `element_type`.

array_shape.description: Full native shape of the stored array, in the order the store holds it: the first axis is the array's length and the trailing axes end with `element_shape`. Static types are `[length, *element_shape]`; a deterministic forecast stacks windows as `[horizon_count, count, *element_shape]`; probabilistic and scenarios forecasts add a percentile or scenario axis in front of that. Optional, and redundant for the static types, where it is exactly `[length] + element_shape`. It earns its place on the forecasts, whose array layout is a convention the producing package owns rather than a rule this layer enforces, so the stored geometry cannot be reconstructed from `horizon`, `count`, `percentiles`, and `scenario_count` alone. A consumer that has it should prefer it; one that does not falls back to those fields, which is exact for the static types and a best effort for the forecasts.

association_id.description: Surrogate id of this association, minted by the store that holds it. Assigned once when the association is created and never changed: renaming the series or reassigning its owner leaves it alone, so a consumer may persist it as a durable reference. Ids are never reused, and they are store-local — resolve one against the same store the document was exported from, not against an independently built store. Assigned by the store, never by a document author.

component_field.description: The field on the owning component or supplemental attribute whose value these values are the time-varying form of (e.g. max_active_power, rating). Free-form: it names a field in the consumer's own object model. Records what the values are for, where `name` only says which series they are.

data_hash.description: Content hash of the stored array: SHA-256, hex-encoded. Optional — not every producer computes it.

element_shape.description: Per-step element shape: the trailing dims after time. An empty array means a scalar element.

element_type.description: What one timestep's values mean and how they are laid out. The physical dtype of the stored bytes derives from this and is not recorded separately. Unlike `units` and `quantity_kind` this is not a user-facing label — the writing package derives it from the array.

features.description: User-defined key/value tags that are part of the series' identity: two series differing only by a feature are distinct series. Feature names that collide with a field of a series or of the tuple addressing one are rejected.

length.description: Number of timesteps. Together with `name` this is what identifies the series: its explicit, strictly-increasing timestamp vector lives in the store, content-addressed so that many irregular series sharing one time axis store it once.

name.description: Time series name (e.g. max_active_power). Part of the series' identity, and often carrying a disambiguating suffix; `component_field` records what the values are for.

owner_category.description: Whether the owner is a component or a supplemental attribute.

owner_id.description: ID of the owning component or supplemental attribute. The producing data layer allocates both from one id stream, so an `owner_id` never collides across the two categories; `owner_category` remains required because the store's catalog contract still supports independent streams from other producers, and it is still the store's disambiguator.

owner_type.description: Type name of the owning entity. Descriptive, not part of the series' identity.

per_unit_of.description: The field on the owning component that the values are a fraction of when `unit_system` is COMPONENT_BASE (e.g. base_power, storage_capacity). Completes the per-unit declaration: it names which of the owner's fields converts the values back to natural units, so a consumer need not know the owner's conventions. Free-form: it names a field in the consumer's own object model, and nothing here checks it against `unit_system`. Not part of the series' identity.

quantity_kind.description: Kind of physical quantity the values measure (e.g. ActivePower, ReactivePower, ElectricalEnergy). Coarser than `units` but finer than a dimension: ActivePower, ReactivePower, and ApparentPower share the dimension {M:1,L:2,T:-3}, so a dimension cannot tell them apart and a quantity kind can. It is also the only record of what the values measure when `unit_system` is a per-unit basis.

time_reference.description: How this series' timestamps were spelled, so a read hands back what the write declared instead of relabelling everything UTC. Absent means unspecified, which is not a claim the timestamps were written as UTC.

time_series_type.description: Discriminator. Fixed to NonSequentialTimeSeries for this schema, pinned with `const` to match this repo's existing discriminators (Core/common.json's `curve_type`), which generate a plain string literal in both toolchains.

timestamps_uri.description: Locator for this series' explicit timestamp vector, unique within one store — `uri`'s counterpart for the time axis, with the same contract: no required format, never parsed or interpreted here, and resolved by the backing store (infrastore uses the axis's content hash, the same value it keys the shared vector under). A locator rather than the vector itself because the axis is shared: a cohort of irregular series on one axis names it once each, where inlining the timestamps would repeat the whole vector per row. Optional, so a producer that predates it is still valid, and absent from the other five types, which have no explicit axis. Without it a document cannot say which of the store's axes a row sits on, and the row cannot be reconstructed from the document — the store cannot infer it either, since arrays are content-addressed and two irregular series with identical values on different axes share one stored array. A consumer restoring rows from a document therefore requires it.

unit_system.description: Basis the series values are already expressed in. A declaration, not a conversion: nothing here rescales values, and converting a COMPONENT_BASE series back to natural units needs the owning component's field that `per_unit_of` names. Absent means unspecified, which is deliberately not the same as NATURAL_UNITS.

units.description: Unit label for the series values. Set by whoever creates the series and returned unchanged; not part of the series' identity, so two series differing only in this label are duplicates. Meaningless on its own when `unit_system` is a per-unit basis, where the values are dimensionless. By convention drawn from the unit vocabulary in Core/units.json, though this field is a free-text label the store does not validate against it.

uri.description: Locator for the dense data, unique within one store. No required format — typically a file path or an HDF5 dataset path; the backing store decides what it means and resolves it (infrastore uses its content hash as this value). Never parsed or interpreted here. This layer records where the values are, never the values.

Probabilistic.description: A probabilistic forecast: per-percentile, per-window horizon arrays. Adds a percentile axis in front of the deterministic layout.

application_data.description: Opaque, package-owned payload (typically JSON) carried verbatim for an application to reconstruct its own domain objects. Never parsed or interpreted here, and end users are not expected to set it. Element typing does not belong here — that is `element_type`.

array_shape.description: Full native shape of the stored array, in the order the store holds it: the first axis is the array's length and the trailing axes end with `element_shape`. Static types are `[length, *element_shape]`; a deterministic forecast stacks windows as `[horizon_count, count, *element_shape]`; probabilistic and scenarios forecasts add a percentile or scenario axis in front of that. Optional, and redundant for the static types, where it is exactly `[length] + element_shape`. It earns its place on the forecasts, whose array layout is a convention the producing package owns rather than a rule this layer enforces, so the stored geometry cannot be reconstructed from `horizon`, `count`, `percentiles`, and `scenario_count` alone. A consumer that has it should prefer it; one that does not falls back to those fields, which is exact for the static types and a best effort for the forecasts.

association_id.description: Surrogate id of this association, minted by the store that holds it. Assigned once when the association is created and never changed: renaming the series or reassigning its owner leaves it alone, so a consumer may persist it as a durable reference. Ids are never reused, and they are store-local — resolve one against the same store the document was exported from, not against an independently built store. Assigned by the store, never by a document author.

component_field.description: The field on the owning component or supplemental attribute whose value these values are the time-varying form of (e.g. max_active_power, rating). Free-form: it names a field in the consumer's own object model. Records what the values are for, where `name` only says which series they are.

count.description: Number of forecast windows. Descriptive, not part of the series' identity.

data_hash.description: Content hash of the stored array: SHA-256, hex-encoded. Optional — not every producer computes it.

element_shape.description: Per-step element shape: the trailing dims after time. An empty array means a scalar element.

element_type.description: What one timestep's values mean and how they are laid out. The physical dtype of the stored bytes derives from this and is not recorded separately. Unlike `units` and `quantity_kind` this is not a user-facing label — the writing package derives it from the array.

features.description: User-defined key/value tags that are part of the series' identity: two series differing only by a feature are distinct series. Feature names that collide with a field of a series or of the tuple addressing one are rejected.

horizon.description: Length of one forecast window. Descriptive, not part of the series' identity.

initial_timestamp.description: Start of the first forecast window. Written in one of two RFC 3339 forms, with at most 3 fractional-second digits: `date-time`, with `Z` or a UTC offset, names an instant; `date-time-local`, with no offset, is a wall clock and names no instant. `time_reference` fixes the form: `zoneless` requires `date-time-local`, `utc` requires a zero offset, and a fixed offset or an IANA zone requires `date-time`. With no `time_reference`, either form is accepted and none is assumed.

interval.description: Step between the start of consecutive forecast windows. Part of the series' identity: two forecasts of one variable at the same resolution but different intervals — a day-ahead and a real-time forecast — are distinct series. `PT0S` is the canonical interval of a single-window forecast, which has no second window to step to.

interval_alignment.description: Position of each timestamp in the period it represents.

name.description: Time series name (e.g. max_active_power). Part of the series' identity, and often carrying a disambiguating suffix; `component_field` records what the values are for.

owner_category.description: Whether the owner is a component or a supplemental attribute.

owner_id.description: ID of the owning component or supplemental attribute. The producing data layer allocates both from one id stream, so an `owner_id` never collides across the two categories; `owner_category` remains required because the store's catalog contract still supports independent streams from other producers, and it is still the store's disambiguator.

owner_type.description: Type name of the owning entity. Descriptive, not part of the series' identity.

per_unit_of.description: The field on the owning component that the values are a fraction of when `unit_system` is COMPONENT_BASE (e.g. base_power, storage_capacity). Completes the per-unit declaration: it names which of the owner's fields converts the values back to natural units, so a consumer need not know the owner's conventions. Free-form: it names a field in the consumer's own object model, and nothing here checks it against `unit_system`. Not part of the series' identity.

percentiles.description: The percentiles this forecast carries, one per leading axis entry of the stored array.

quantity_kind.description: Kind of physical quantity the values measure (e.g. ActivePower, ReactivePower, ElectricalEnergy). Coarser than `units` but finer than a dimension: ActivePower, ReactivePower, and ApparentPower share the dimension {M:1,L:2,T:-3}, so a dimension cannot tell them apart and a quantity kind can. It is also the only record of what the values measure when `unit_system` is a per-unit basis.

resolution.description: Cadence within a forecast window. Always present for a forecast, and part of the series' identity.

time_reference.description: How this series' timestamps were spelled, so a read hands back what the write declared instead of relabelling everything UTC. Absent means unspecified, which is not a claim the timestamps were written as UTC.

time_series_type.description: Discriminator. Fixed to Probabilistic for this schema, pinned with `const` to match this repo's existing discriminators (Core/common.json's `curve_type`), which generate a plain string literal in both toolchains.

unit_system.description: Basis the series values are already expressed in. A declaration, not a conversion: nothing here rescales values, and converting a COMPONENT_BASE series back to natural units needs the owning component's field that `per_unit_of` names. Absent means unspecified, which is deliberately not the same as NATURAL_UNITS.

units.description: Unit label for the series values. Set by whoever creates the series and returned unchanged; not part of the series' identity, so two series differing only in this label are duplicates. Meaningless on its own when `unit_system` is a per-unit basis, where the values are dimensionless. By convention drawn from the unit vocabulary in Core/units.json, though this field is a free-text label the store does not validate against it.

uri.description: Locator for the dense data, unique within one store. No required format — typically a file path or an HDF5 dataset path; the backing store decides what it means and resolves it (infrastore uses its content hash as this value). Never parsed or interpreted here. This layer records where the values are, never the values.

Scenarios.description: A scenarios forecast: per-scenario, per-window horizon arrays. Adds a scenario axis in front of the deterministic layout.

application_data.description: Opaque, package-owned payload (typically JSON) carried verbatim for an application to reconstruct its own domain objects. Never parsed or interpreted here, and end users are not expected to set it. Element typing does not belong here — that is `element_type`.

array_shape.description: Full native shape of the stored array, in the order the store holds it: the first axis is the array's length and the trailing axes end with `element_shape`. Static types are `[length, *element_shape]`; a deterministic forecast stacks windows as `[horizon_count, count, *element_shape]`; probabilistic and scenarios forecasts add a percentile or scenario axis in front of that. Optional, and redundant for the static types, where it is exactly `[length] + element_shape`. It earns its place on the forecasts, whose array layout is a convention the producing package owns rather than a rule this layer enforces, so the stored geometry cannot be reconstructed from `horizon`, `count`, `percentiles`, and `scenario_count` alone. A consumer that has it should prefer it; one that does not falls back to those fields, which is exact for the static types and a best effort for the forecasts.

association_id.description: Surrogate id of this association, minted by the store that holds it. Assigned once when the association is created and never changed: renaming the series or reassigning its owner leaves it alone, so a consumer may persist it as a durable reference. Ids are never reused, and they are store-local — resolve one against the same store the document was exported from, not against an independently built store. Assigned by the store, never by a document author.

component_field.description: The field on the owning component or supplemental attribute whose value these values are the time-varying form of (e.g. max_active_power, rating). Free-form: it names a field in the consumer's own object model. Records what the values are for, where `name` only says which series they are.

count.description: Number of forecast windows. Descriptive, not part of the series' identity.

data_hash.description: Content hash of the stored array: SHA-256, hex-encoded. Optional — not every producer computes it.

element_shape.description: Per-step element shape: the trailing dims after time. An empty array means a scalar element.

element_type.description: What one timestep's values mean and how they are laid out. The physical dtype of the stored bytes derives from this and is not recorded separately. Unlike `units` and `quantity_kind` this is not a user-facing label — the writing package derives it from the array.

features.description: User-defined key/value tags that are part of the series' identity: two series differing only by a feature are distinct series. Feature names that collide with a field of a series or of the tuple addressing one are rejected.

horizon.description: Length of one forecast window. Descriptive, not part of the series' identity.

initial_timestamp.description: Start of the first forecast window. Written in one of two RFC 3339 forms, with at most 3 fractional-second digits: `date-time`, with `Z` or a UTC offset, names an instant; `date-time-local`, with no offset, is a wall clock and names no instant. `time_reference` fixes the form: `zoneless` requires `date-time-local`, `utc` requires a zero offset, and a fixed offset or an IANA zone requires `date-time`. With no `time_reference`, either form is accepted and none is assumed.

interval.description: Step between the start of consecutive forecast windows. Part of the series' identity: two forecasts of one variable at the same resolution but different intervals — a day-ahead and a real-time forecast — are distinct series. `PT0S` is the canonical interval of a single-window forecast, which has no second window to step to.

interval_alignment.description: Position of each timestamp in the period it represents.

name.description: Time series name (e.g. max_active_power). Part of the series' identity, and often carrying a disambiguating suffix; `component_field` records what the values are for.

owner_category.description: Whether the owner is a component or a supplemental attribute.

owner_id.description: ID of the owning component or supplemental attribute. The producing data layer allocates both from one id stream, so an `owner_id` never collides across the two categories; `owner_category` remains required because the store's catalog contract still supports independent streams from other producers, and it is still the store's disambiguator.

owner_type.description: Type name of the owning entity. Descriptive, not part of the series' identity.

per_unit_of.description: The field on the owning component that the values are a fraction of when `unit_system` is COMPONENT_BASE (e.g. base_power, storage_capacity). Completes the per-unit declaration: it names which of the owner's fields converts the values back to natural units, so a consumer need not know the owner's conventions. Free-form: it names a field in the consumer's own object model, and nothing here checks it against `unit_system`. Not part of the series' identity.

quantity_kind.description: Kind of physical quantity the values measure (e.g. ActivePower, ReactivePower, ElectricalEnergy). Coarser than `units` but finer than a dimension: ActivePower, ReactivePower, and ApparentPower share the dimension {M:1,L:2,T:-3}, so a dimension cannot tell them apart and a quantity kind can. It is also the only record of what the values measure when `unit_system` is a per-unit basis.

resolution.description: Cadence within a forecast window. Always present for a forecast, and part of the series' identity.

scenario_count.description: Number of scenarios, one per leading axis entry of the stored array. The store's catalog has no column for this and reads it off the array's shape; it is recorded explicitly here because this layer carries no array.

time_reference.description: How this series' timestamps were spelled, so a read hands back what the write declared instead of relabelling everything UTC. Absent means unspecified, which is not a claim the timestamps were written as UTC.

time_series_type.description: Discriminator. Fixed to Scenarios for this schema, pinned with `const` to match this repo's existing discriminators (Core/common.json's `curve_type`), which generate a plain string literal in both toolchains.

unit_system.description: Basis the series values are already expressed in. A declaration, not a conversion: nothing here rescales values, and converting a COMPONENT_BASE series back to natural units needs the owning component's field that `per_unit_of` names. Absent means unspecified, which is deliberately not the same as NATURAL_UNITS.

units.description: Unit label for the series values. Set by whoever creates the series and returned unchanged; not part of the series' identity, so two series differing only in this label are duplicates. Meaningless on its own when `unit_system` is a per-unit basis, where the values are dimensionless. By convention drawn from the unit vocabulary in Core/units.json, though this field is a free-text label the store does not validate against it.

uri.description: Locator for the dense data, unique within one store. No required format — typically a file path or an HDF5 dataset path; the backing store decides what it means and resolves it (infrastore uses its content hash as this value). Never parsed or interpreted here. This layer records where the values are, never the values.

SingleTimeSeries.description: A static time series on a regular grid: values at `initial_timestamp + k * resolution`. One of a closed set of six canonical time series types owned by the data layer. This schema records the association and its metadata; the dense values live in the store named by `uri`.

application_data.description: Opaque, package-owned payload (typically JSON) carried verbatim for an application to reconstruct its own domain objects. Never parsed or interpreted here, and end users are not expected to set it. Element typing does not belong here — that is `element_type`.

array_shape.description: Full native shape of the stored array, in the order the store holds it: the first axis is the array's length and the trailing axes end with `element_shape`. Static types are `[length, *element_shape]`; a deterministic forecast stacks windows as `[horizon_count, count, *element_shape]`; probabilistic and scenarios forecasts add a percentile or scenario axis in front of that. Optional, and redundant for the static types, where it is exactly `[length] + element_shape`. It earns its place on the forecasts, whose array layout is a convention the producing package owns rather than a rule this layer enforces, so the stored geometry cannot be reconstructed from `horizon`, `count`, `percentiles`, and `scenario_count` alone. A consumer that has it should prefer it; one that does not falls back to those fields, which is exact for the static types and a best effort for the forecasts.

association_id.description: Surrogate id of this association, minted by the store that holds it. Assigned once when the association is created and never changed: renaming the series or reassigning its owner leaves it alone, so a consumer may persist it as a durable reference. Ids are never reused, and they are store-local — resolve one against the same store the document was exported from, not against an independently built store. Assigned by the store, never by a document author.

component_field.description: The field on the owning component or supplemental attribute whose value these values are the time-varying form of (e.g. max_active_power, rating). Free-form: it names a field in the consumer's own object model. Records what the values are for, where `name` only says which series they are.

data_hash.description: Content hash of the stored array: SHA-256, hex-encoded. Optional — not every producer computes it.

element_shape.description: Per-step element shape: the trailing dims after time. An empty array means a scalar element.

element_type.description: What one timestep's values mean and how they are laid out. The physical dtype of the stored bytes derives from this and is not recorded separately. Unlike `units` and `quantity_kind` this is not a user-facing label — the writing package derives it from the array.

features.description: User-defined key/value tags that are part of the series' identity: two series differing only by a feature are distinct series. Feature names that collide with a field of a series or of the tuple addressing one are rejected.

initial_timestamp.description: First timestamp of the regular grid; every later step lands at `initial_timestamp + k * resolution`. The store's floor is one millisecond, matching Julia's millisecond-precision DateTime. Written in one of two RFC 3339 forms, with at most 3 fractional-second digits: `date-time`, with `Z` or a UTC offset, names an instant; `date-time-local`, with no offset, is a wall clock and names no instant. `time_reference` fixes the form: `zoneless` requires `date-time-local`, `utc` requires a zero offset, and a fixed offset or an IANA zone requires `date-time`. With no `time_reference`, either form is accepted and none is assumed.

interval_alignment.description: Position of each timestamp in the period it represents.

name.description: Time series name (e.g. max_active_power). Part of the series' identity, and often carrying a disambiguating suffix; `component_field` records what the values are for.

owner_category.description: Whether the owner is a component or a supplemental attribute.

owner_id.description: ID of the owning component or supplemental attribute. The producing data layer allocates both from one id stream, so an `owner_id` never collides across the two categories; `owner_category` remains required because the store's catalog contract still supports independent streams from other producers, and it is still the store's disambiguator.

owner_type.description: Type name of the owning entity. Descriptive, not part of the series' identity.

per_unit_of.description: The field on the owning component that the values are a fraction of when `unit_system` is COMPONENT_BASE (e.g. base_power, storage_capacity). Completes the per-unit declaration: it names which of the owner's fields converts the values back to natural units, so a consumer need not know the owner's conventions. Free-form: it names a field in the consumer's own object model, and nothing here checks it against `unit_system`. Not part of the series' identity.

quantity_kind.description: Kind of physical quantity the values measure (e.g. ActivePower, ReactivePower, ElectricalEnergy). Coarser than `units` but finer than a dimension: ActivePower, ReactivePower, and ApparentPower share the dimension {M:1,L:2,T:-3}, so a dimension cannot tell them apart and a quantity kind can. It is also the only record of what the values measure when `unit_system` is a per-unit basis.

resolution.description: Cadence of the regular grid. Always present for a SingleTimeSeries, and part of the series' identity.

time_reference.description: How this series' timestamps were spelled, so a read hands back what the write declared instead of relabelling everything UTC. Absent means unspecified, which is not a claim the timestamps were written as UTC.

time_series_type.description: Discriminator. Fixed to SingleTimeSeries for this schema, pinned with `const` to match this repo's existing discriminators (Core/common.json's `curve_type`), which generate a plain string literal in both toolchains.

unit_system.description: Basis the series values are already expressed in. A declaration, not a conversion: nothing here rescales values, and converting a COMPONENT_BASE series back to natural units needs the owning component's field that `per_unit_of` names. Absent means unspecified, which is deliberately not the same as NATURAL_UNITS.

units.description: Unit label for the series values. Set by whoever creates the series and returned unchanged; not part of the series' identity, so two series differing only in this label are duplicates. Meaningless on its own when `unit_system` is a per-unit basis, where the values are dimensionless. By convention drawn from the unit vocabulary in Core/units.json, though this field is a free-text label the store does not validate against it.

uri.description: Locator for the dense data, unique within one store. No required format — typically a file path or an HDF5 dataset path; the backing store decides what it means and resolves it (infrastore uses its content hash as this value). Never parsed or interpreted here. This layer records where the values are, never the values.

StandardLoad.description:
A voltage-dependent ZIP load, most commonly used for dynamics modeling.

A `StandardLoad` breaks the ZIP into three pieces: Z (constant impedance), I (constant current), and P (constant power), according to `P = P_P * V^0 + P_I * V^1 + P_Z * V^2` for active power and `Q = Q_P * V^0 + Q_I * V^1 + Q_Z * V^2` for reactive power. (Voltage V is in per unit.)

For an alternative exponential formulation of the ZIP model, see `ExponentialLoad`. For a simpler load model with no voltage dependency, see `PowerLoad`.

A thermal generator, such as a fossil fuel and nuclear generator.

This is a standard representation with options to include a minimum up time, minimum down time, and ramp limits. For a more detailed representation of the start-up and shut-down processes, including hot starts, see `ThermalMultiStart`.

ThreeWindingTransformer.description: A three-winding transformer, modeled as an equivalent star: each referenced `TransformerCircuit` connects a terminal bus to the star (hidden) bus and carries that winding's series electrical data; availability is circuit-level. The pairwise measured impedances `r_12`/`x_12`, `r_23`/`x_23`, `r_31`/`x_31` (PSS/E CZ = 1, each in pu on the corresponding `base_power_12`/`base_power_23`/`base_power_31` and referenced to the first-index winding's base voltage) are optional and must be set together or all be absent; the star-leg impedances derived from them at parse time live on the circuits and are not synced back. Power-flow and Ybus assembly read the per-circuit star-leg impedances, not the pairwise fields. The model is described in Chapter 3.6 of J.D. Glover, M.S. Sarma and T. Overbye: Power Systems Analysis and Design.

TimeReference.description: How a series' timestamps were spelled, recorded so a read hands back what the write declared instead of relabelling every series UTC. Four forms share one string, and are unambiguous because a zone name that would read as either literal or as an offset is rejected: `utc`; `zoneless` for a wall clock, which names no instant; a fixed UTC offset (`-07:00`, `+0530`, `+05`); or an IANA zone name (`America/Denver`). Only the name's shape is checked here — whether a zone exists is a tz-database question, and the store records the name either way. A spelling, not a grid: it does not change what a calendar `resolution` steps on, and a series on a local-clock grid is a NonSequentialTimeSeries. Descriptive, so two series differing only in it are duplicates rather than distinct series, but not inert — a query's bounds must match the series' spelling, and the zoneless series form their own group.

TimeSeriesAssociation.description:
Metadata linking one time series to the component or supplemental attribute that owns it — the JSON form of a row in the store's `time_series_associations` catalog table. A closed set of six canonical types owned by the data layer: two static (SingleTimeSeries on a regular grid, NonSequentialTimeSeries on explicit irregular timestamps) and four forecasts. The type decides which timing fields the row carries, which is why each is its own schema rather than one row with everything nullable.

Dense values never appear here. `uri` names the store location that holds them; `data_hash` optionally carries a content hash of that array. A NonSequentialTimeSeries adds `timestamps_uri`, the same kind of locator for its explicit time axis, which is likewise stored rather than carried. Content hashes themselves (features_hash, timestamps_hash) remain store-internal and deliberately absent — a locator names where something is, which is not the same as exposing the store's own address for it.
TimeSeriesAssociation.title: TimeSeriesAssociation

TimeSeriesFeatureValue.description: One feature value. Four kinds, matching the backing store's feature-value type: int, float, bool, str. `anyOf` rather than `oneOf` is required, not stylistic: JSON Schema's `integer` is a subset of `number`, so an integer instance matches both branches and `oneOf` — which demands exactly one match — would reject every integer feature. A float feature is compared and hashed by its bit pattern rather than by IEEE comparison, so 0.0 and -0.0 are two different series; NaN and negative zero are rejected on write because the catalog cannot store either faithfully.
TimeSeriesFeatureValue.title: TimeSeriesFeatureValue

TimeSeriesFeatures.description: User-defined key/value tags forming part of a series' identity. A map, matching the backing store's feature-map type (a BTreeMap whose sort order is load-bearing, because the hash of the feature map keys the catalog's uniqueness index). The excluded property names each already name a field of a time series or of the tuple that addresses one: consumers routinely spread a feature map into keyword arguments, where a feature called `name` or `resolution` would shadow the real field and silently change what a query means. The comparison is exact and case-sensitive — `resolution` is reserved, `Resolution` is not.

TransformerCircuit.description:
The data defining one modeled arc of a transformer.

A `TwoWindingTransformer` has one circuit; a `ThreeWindingTransformer` has three, each connecting a terminal bus to the star bus. Circuit `available` is the single source of truth for availability; the owning transformer derives its availability from its circuits. `r`/`x` are the circuit impedance (for a two-winding transformer, the series impedance; for a three-winding transformer, the star-leg equivalent), in pu (device base) on `base_power` referenced to `base_voltage_primary`. Tap-changer / phase-shifter control is described by the flat control fields: `control_objective = UNDEFINED` means the circuit has no control block. Each objective selects exactly one actuator band (`tap_ratio_limits` or `phase_angle_limits`) and one target band (`controlled_voltage_limits`, `controlled_reactive_power_flow_limits` or `controlled_active_power_flow_limits`); every other band is `null`. For a `TwoWindingTransformer`, the single circuit's `base_power` is the transformer's device base.

active_power_flow.description: Initial condition of active power flow through this circuit. Units: per power_units — NATURAL_UNITS: MW, COMPONENT_BASE: pu .

alpha.description: Initial condition of phase shift across this circuit. Units: rad.

arc.description: An `Arc` defining this circuit `from` a terminal bus `to` the transformer's other terminal or star bus.

available.description: Indicator of whether this circuit is connected and online.

base_power.description: Base power for per unitization of this circuit. Units: MVA.

base_voltage_primary.description: Primary (from) terminal-side base voltage; the reference voltage for this circuit's per-unit impedance. Units: kV.

base_voltage_secondary.description: Secondary (to) terminal-side base voltage. For a three-winding transformer this defaults to the primary base voltage at parse time. Units: kV.

control_objective.description: Tap-changer / phase-shifter control objective (PSS/E COD). `UNDEFINED` means this circuit has no control block.

controlled_active_power_flow_limits.description: Regulated active-power-flow target band (PSS/E VMA/VMI). `null` unless `control_objective` selects it. Units: per power_units — NATURAL_UNITS: MW, COMPONENT_BASE: pu .

controlled_reactive_power_flow_limits.description: Regulated reactive-power-flow target band (PSS/E VMA/VMI). `null` unless `control_objective` selects it. Units: per power_units — NATURAL_UNITS: MVAr, COMPONENT_BASE: pu .

controlled_voltage_limits.description: Regulated-voltage target band (PSS/E VMA/VMI), per unit of the regulated bus's base voltage. `null` unless `control_objective` selects it. Units: pu.

id.description: Unique integer identifier for this component.

operational_flow_limit.description: Operator-set minimum and maximum flow in each direction, applied in addition to `rating`. Absent means no operational limit. Units: per power_units — NATURAL_UNITS: MW, COMPONENT_BASE: pu .

parameter_units.description: Unit basis for this circuit's impedance fields (r, x).

phase_angle_limits.description: Phase-shift actuator band (PSS/E RMA/RMI when the objective moves the angle). `null` unless `control_objective` selects it. Units: rad.

power_units.description: Unit basis for this component's power-family fields (active/reactive/apparent power, ratings, limits, ramp rates). COMPONENT_BASE: per unit on this component's own base_power. NATURAL_UNITS: the field's physical unit.

r.description: Circuit resistance. Units: per parameter_units — NATURAL_UNITS: ohm, COMPONENT_BASE: pu .

rating.description: Thermal rating. Units: per power_units — NATURAL_UNITS: MVA, COMPONENT_BASE: pu .

rating_b.description: Short-term thermal rating (Rate B in PSS/E), the flow allowed for a limited time, such as after a contingency. Absent means no short-term rating. Units: per power_units — NATURAL_UNITS: MVA, COMPONENT_BASE: pu .

rating_c.description: Emergency thermal rating (Rate C in PSS/E), the highest flow allowed for a brief period. Absent means no emergency rating. Units: per power_units — NATURAL_UNITS: MVA, COMPONENT_BASE: pu .

reactive_power_flow.description: Initial condition of reactive power flow through this circuit. Units: per power_units — NATURAL_UNITS: MVAr, COMPONENT_BASE: pu .

regulated_bus.description: ID of the bus whose voltage this circuit's tap changer regulates (PSS/E CONT), within `controlled_voltage_limits`. It may be an end of `arc` or a remote bus. Used only when `control_objective` is `VOLTAGE` or `VOLTAGE_DISABLED`; null otherwise, or when no regulated bus is stated.

regulated_bus_orientation.description: Direction the tap adjustment assumes for `regulated_bus`, replacing the sign of PSS/E CONT. Stated only when `regulated_bus` is not an end of `arc`; `UNDEFINED` when it is an end of `arc` or null, because the connections already give the direction.

tap.description: Normalized tap changer position for voltage control, varying between 0 and 2, with 1 centered at the nominal voltage. Units: 1.

tap_ratio_limits.description: Tap-ratio actuator band (PSS/E RMA/RMI) when `control_objective` moves the tap; `null` otherwise. Under the tap-moving objectives it may be omitted and then defaults to 0.9 to 1.1, PSS/E's own RMI/RMA defaults, which is why it is the one band the conditional blocks do not require. Units: 1.

x.description: Circuit reactance. Units: per parameter_units — NATURAL_UNITS: ohm, COMPONENT_BASE: pu .

TransformerControlObjective.description: Control objective of a transformer tap changer or phase shifter: a fixed tap position with no automatic adjustment (`FIXED`), or regulation of voltage magnitude at the controlled bus, reactive power flow, active power flow, asymmetric active power flow, or a DC line. Each regulating objective has a paired `_DISABLED` value naming the same control block while it is out of service, and `UNDEFINED` means no control objective is stated.
TransformerControlObjective.title: TransformerControlObjective

TransformerRegulationOrientation.description: Which end of a transformer circuit's `arc` the tap adjustment treats the regulated bus as lying on, when the regulated bus is not an end of the arc: a remote bus, or another winding's terminal of a three-winding transformer. It sets the direction the tap moves to raise that bus's voltage (PSS/E sign of CONT). The `from` end is the tapped winding. UNDEFINED: the regulated bus is an end of the arc, so the connections give the direction, or there is no regulated bus. FROM: adjust as if the regulated bus lies on the `from` side (PSS/E negative CONT). TO: adjust as if it lies on the `to` side (PSS/E positive CONT).
TransformerRegulationOrientation.title: TransformerRegulationOrientation

A two-winding transformer connecting two buses.

description:
The serialized form of a whole power system: every component, the association tables that link them, and the name of the HDF5 sidecar holding time series values. This is the interchange format between producers (the producing parsers and the data model library) and consumers (the data model library, the relational mirror, non-Julia clients), so the shape is defined here rather than by convention in each producer.

There is no document-level unit system or base power: every value in the document is interpretable from its own component blob alone. A discriminated field is resolved against a basis-selector property recorded on that same blob (`power_units`, `parameter_units`, `energy_units`, and the like) and, for a COMPONENT_BASE reading, against that blob's own `base_power` — never a document-wide table. A field with a fixed `x-unit` is already in its natural unit and needs no basis at all. This applies uniformly to component blobs and to any embedded cost payload's own `power_units`; a time series association's `unit_system` likewise governs only that one series.

Deliberately excluded from openapi-generator: `components` is a map from type name to an array of heterogeneous component objects, which the generated Julia client cannot express as typed buckets. The hand-written container in the generated core model package (`src/document.jl`) is the single Julia representation, and its fields are checked against this file. This schema remains authoritative for every other language binding.

Time series *values* never appear here. `time_series_associations` carries the metadata rows and `time_series_storage_file` names the sidecar; reading or writing that file is the consumer's job.

combined_cycle_associations.description: Links a CombinedCycleBlock plant to a CT or CA unit, identifying which HRSG the unit feeds into or receives from.

components.description: Components grouped by type name, e.g. `{"ACBus": [...], "ThermalStandard": [...]}`. The key is the referenced schema's `title`. Keys are emitted in sorted order so output is deterministic. Every type present must be one the consumer can convert: a consumer encountering an unknown type name must fail rather than skip it. A dynamic injection (e.g. `DynamicGenerator`) is a component with no bus of its own: a non-null `dynamic_injector` on a static injection device must name a dynamic injection's `id`, each dynamic injection must be named by exactly one static device, and the two must have the same `name`. A dynamic injection names its function blocks (`excitation_system_dynamics`, `filter`, ...) by `id`; each must name a standard model of that function block class (e.g. `excitation_system_dynamics` names an `ExcitationSystemDynamics` model such as `SEXS`), and each function block must be named by exactly one dynamic injection. A reader checks these links after decoding, with one id lookup per reference.

description.description: Optional free-text description of the system.

ext.description: Source data that no schema field claims, keyed by the stringified component id it belongs to. Only values genuinely unclaimed by any schema field may appear here; a producer must never mirror a value that also landed in a schema field. An absent or empty `ext` means the producer mapped everything. A consumer must consume keys via a declared ignore list: a listed key is skipped, an unlisted key is an error naming the key and the component id — never a silent drop.

name.description: Optional system name.

plant_associations.description: Links a power plant supplemental attribute (ThermalPowerPlant, HydroPowerPlant, RenewablePowerPlant, CombinedCycleFractional) to a generating unit and the group it belongs to within the plant: shafts, penstocks, PCCs, or exclusion groups.

schema_version.description: Version of the schema release that wrote this document, without a leading `v`. A reader compares it with its own before decoding anything else; the comparison rule is defined once, in the schema repository's versioning document.

service_associations.description: Links a service to one component that contributes to it. One row per (service, member) pair.

supplemental_attribute_associations.description: Links each plain supplemental attribute (e.g. EmissionsData, GeographicInfo) to the entity it describes. One row per (attribute, entity) pair. Plant, combined-cycle, and service memberships are carried by their own arrays below, not here.

supplemental_attributes.description: Supplemental attributes in one flat array rather than bucketed by type: nothing iterates them per type, and `supplemental_attribute_associations` carries both the link and the `attribute_type` discriminator a consumer needs to pick a converter.

time_series_associations.description: Time series metadata rows, one per (series, owner) association. Each row names the store holding its values in its own `address`; `time_series_storage_file` remains the document-level sidecar name.

time_series_storage_file.description: Basename of the HDF5 sidecar holding time series values, or null when the system has no time series. A name, not a path: the file is resolved relative to the document, so a document and its sidecar can be moved together.

trading_hub_associations.description: Links a trading hub to one associated entity: a member bus or a market transaction settling at the hub. One row per (hub, member) pair. Optional, defaulting to empty: unlike the association arrays that have been required since the format existed, this one was added later, so documents written before it exist and omit it.

voltage_control_associations.description: Links a voltage control group (VoltageDroopControl or ReactivePowerSharing) to one member device with its relative reactive power weight and, for a two-terminal member, the converter terminal. One row per (control, member). Optional, defaulting to empty, like `trading_hub_associations`: documents written before it exist and omit it.
